sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Pachamama** ​(*pachamama*) ‌— Earth, ‌Harvest, ​Mother ​· ​Mother ​Earth — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Incan tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Earth, ​Harvest, ​Mother". The ​name ‌means ​"Mother ‌Earth".

**Pachamama** ​is ‌earth, ​harvest, ‌mother. ​The name ‌means ​"Mother ​Earth" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​incan ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**Pachamama** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/pachamama/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*pachamama* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation survives ‌for ​this name; ​**Pachamama** ​is a ​scholarly transliteration ​of ‌the reconstructed ​spoken form. ​Etymologically ‌the name ​means ‌"Mother Earth".

​The ASCII ‌form ​*pachamama* survives ​only because ​the ​early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry diacritics; ‌it ​is a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. ‌The Unicode ​restoration **Pachamama** ​recovers ‌the full ‌diacritic detail ‌of ​the scholarly ​transliteration ‌directly in ​the address ​bar. ‌The restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form would ​lose, ​which places ​the name ‌in ‌Tier 2.

​The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ​runs:

- ​**p** ‌→ **P** ‌— Same
‌- ‌**a** → ​**a** ‌— Same
​- **c** ​→ ​**c** — ‌Same
- ​**h** ​→ **h** ​— ‌Same
- ​**a** → ​**a** ​— Same
‌- **m** ​→ ‌**m** — ​Same
‌- **a** ​→ **a** ‌— ‌Same
- ​**m** → ​**m** ​— Same
​- ‌**a** → ‌**a** — ​Same

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/pachamama/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**pachamama** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Pachamama.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"pachamama" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Pachamama".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"pachamama" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Pachamama" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Pachamama was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Pachamama ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌Pachamama ‌place ​earth, harvest, ​mother ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌Pachamama appears ​in ‌incan ​tradition as ​earth, ​harvest, mother. ​The ​name's ‌meaning, "Mother ​Earth", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Pachamama ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​Pachamama ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Pachamama ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

sections.label: Archaeology & Material Evidence
sections.purpose: Sites, inscriptions, artifacts, and physical attestations.
sections.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Pachamama ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Pachamama, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​earth ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

sections.label: Meditation & Reflection
sections.purpose: Contemplative or interpretive essay on the figure's enduring meaning.
sections.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Pachamama is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of earth, ​Harvest, ‌Mother ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Mother Earth" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​earth, ‌Harvest, ​Mother ​· ‌Mother Earth.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Pachamama ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*pachamama* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
